questions.question: Work is defined as the dot product of:
questions.explanation: Work W is the scalar product of force F and displacement d. W = F · d = Fd cosθ.

questions.question: The SI unit of work is:
questions.explanation:
The Joule (J) is the SI unit. 1 Joule is the work done when a force of 1 Newton moves an object 1
meter.

questions.question: If the angle between force and displacement is 90°, the work done is:
questions.explanation: When θ = 90°, cos 90° = 0, so W = 0. Hence normal force or centripetal force does no work.

questions.question: A person holding a heavy box and standing still does:
questions.explanation: Even though the person feels tired, displacement is zero. So work done is zero.

questions.question: Work done is negative when the angle between force and displacement is:
questions.explanation: If θ = 180°, cos 180° = -1, so work is negative (e.g., friction opposes motion).

questions.question: The area under a Force–Displacement graph represents:
questions.explanation: The integral F·dx is the area under the force-displacement graph representing work.

questions.question: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: Work is a dot product of vectors, so it is a scalar quantity.

questions.question: Kinetic energy of a body of mass m moving with velocity v is:
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is energy of motion: KE = 1/2 mv².

questions.question: If the velocity of a body is doubled, its kinetic energy becomes:
questions.explanation: KE is proportional to v². If velocity doubles, KE becomes four times.

questions.question: The work-energy theorem states that work done on a body is equal to change in its:
questions.explanation: Work-energy theorem: net work equals change in kinetic energy.

questions.question: Gravitational potential energy is given by:
questions.explanation: Gravitational potential energy: PE = mgh.

questions.question: A force is conservative if work done is:
questions.explanation: Conservative forces depend only on initial and final positions, not path.

questions.question: A non-conservative force is:
questions.explanation: Non-conservative forces like friction convert energy into heat; work depends on path.

questions.question: Total mechanical energy is the sum of:
questions.explanation: Mechanical energy = KE + PE, conserved in absence of friction.

questions.question: In free fall (no resistance), mechanical energy is:
questions.explanation: In free fall, PE converts into KE while total mechanical energy remains constant.

questions.question: Power is the rate of doing:
questions.explanation: Power is rate of doing work: P = W/t.

questions.question: SI unit of power is:
questions.explanation: Watt is the SI unit of power (J/s).

questions.question: 1 horsepower equals:
questions.explanation: 1 horsepower = 746 watts.

questions.question: Power can be expressed as dot product of:
questions.explanation: Power = work/time = force × velocity.

questions.question: A kilowatt-hour (kWh) is a unit of:
questions.explanation: Energy = power × time. Measured in kWh.
